# Occasion and audience

## What this deck is made for

- Occasion: a decision paper, before the build or before a certification
- Audience: `management`
- Length: 20 minutes, without discussion
- What the listeners already know: that information security is a subject, and
  nothing else about the standard

::: {.notes}
This slide is not presented. It stands at the front so that a second presenter
sees in thirty seconds whether the deck fits their appointment. The deck for
the practitioners sits beside it and is a different talk, not a long version of
this one.
:::

# What it is about

## The subject in one sentence

ISO/IEC 27001 asks that information security be steered and not merely done,
and it describes a management system for that.

## Why it concerns the leadership

- Four decisions the standard assigns expressly to top management, and none of
  them can be handed down
- Without those four the system stands still, however much work goes on
  underneath
- The organisation gets certified, not the department

## What a management system means here

- No tool, no software, no project with a closing date
- Arrangements, responsibilities, procedures and records that together bring it
  about that decisions get made, things get done, results get measured and
  things get changed
- The difference from today is usually not that nothing gets done but that
  nobody looks at whether it worked

# The four decisions

## First: the scope

- Which parts, sites, activities and systems belong to it
- What stays outside does not disappear but is not steered
- A narrow scope is allowed and is reached sooner; it then also says less
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 4.3

## Second: the policy and the responsibilities

- An adopted information security policy, carried by the leadership and not
  written by the specialists and signed off
- Named responsibilities, so that a risk belongs to somebody in the end
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 5.2 and 5.3

## Third: the criteria for risks

- Above what size does a risk have to be treated
- Who may approve a risk that remains
- Both get set rather than calculated, and both belong to the leadership
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 6.1.2 and 6.1.3

## Fourth: the resources

- People, time and money, and lastingly rather than once
- The commonest cause of a system that stopped is a role somebody carries on
  top of their full workload
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 7.1

# What the leadership gets back for it

## Four things, regularly

- A statement of which risks the organisation carries, and who approved them
- Numbers that show whether the controls work
- Findings from internal examinations, before a customer or a supervisor finds
  them
- A paper to decide on, on a fixed beat
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 9.1 and 9.3

## What it does not get back

- No assurance that nothing will happen
- No residual risk of zero; anyone shown one is looking at a wrong calculation
  and not at good news

# What to do or decide afterwards

## The paper

- Is a management system to ISO/IEC 27001 built, yes or no
- If yes: which scope, with one sentence of reasoning
- If yes: which person carries the role, with what share of their time
- If yes: is a certification aimed for, and by when
- The certification may stay open; the scope may not, because without it the
  work cannot start
